title: ‘Everyone is scared’: flood-hit Porto Alegre braces for another El Niño

paragraphs.en: In the backstreets of Porto Alegre, a state capital in southern Brazil , you can still see signs of the devastating flood that swept through the city two years ago: scattered debris, waterlogged homes and destroyed businesses.
paragraphs.zh: 在巴西南部州首府阿雷格里港的后街小巷里，仍能看到两年前席卷全城的灾难性洪水的痕迹：散落的废墟、被水浸泡的房屋和被毁的商铺。

paragraphs.en: In May 2024, flooding killed 183 people in the state of Rio Grande do Sul and displaced more than 600,000 . The neighbourhood of Sarandi was one of the hardest-hit parts of Porto Alegre , with water levels reaching up to 5 metres above normal, completely submerging many of its streets.
paragraphs.zh: 2024年5月，南里奥格兰德州洪灾造成183人死亡，60多万人流离失所。萨兰迪街区是阿雷格里港受灾最严重的地区之一，水位一度高出正常水平5米，许多街道被完全淹没。

paragraphs.en: “Most people are still suffering the mental health consequences of the flood,” says Luís Rogério “Jamaika” Machado, a community leader in Sarandi.
paragraphs.zh: “大多数人至今仍承受着洪水带来的心理影响，”萨兰迪的社区领袖路易斯·罗热里奥·“牙买加”·马查多（Luís Rogério “Jamaika” Machado）说。

paragraphs.en: “They lost absolutely everything. Unable to rebuild their houses, most have become deeply depressed.”
paragraphs.zh: “他们失去了一切。由于无力重建家园，大多数人陷入了深深的抑郁。”

paragraphs.en: In June, meteorologists announced the imminent return of El Niño , the naturally occurring phenomenon caused by rising sea-surface temperatures in the equatorial Pacific but the effects of which are greatly aggravated by the climate crisis . El Niño, which disrupts weather patterns across the globe, is likely to cause extreme rainfall and flooding in southern Brazil.
paragraphs.zh: 6月，气象学家宣布厄尔尼诺即将回归。厄尔尼诺是一种由赤道太平洋海面温度上升引发的自然现象，但其影响因气候危机而被大大加剧。厄尔尼诺会扰乱全球天气模式，很可能导致巴西南部出现极端降雨和洪水。

paragraphs.en: Jamaika lives in an urban quilombo , a Brazilian settlement founded by escaped enslaved people or their descendants. Quilombo dos Machado is one of 11 such territories in Porto Alegre and served as a centre of solidarity for the entire Sarandi area during the flood, distributing food, clothing and medical assistance to thousands of families.
paragraphs.zh: “牙买加”住在一个城市“基隆博”（quilombo）社区里，这是巴西由逃亡奴隶或其后代建立的特殊定居点。马查多基隆博是阿雷格里港11个此类社区之一，洪水期间成为整个萨兰迪地区的团结互助中心，向数千个家庭分发食物、衣物和医疗援助。

paragraphs.en: Now Porto Alegre’s flood-hit communities, though still recovering from one of Brazil’s deadliest climate disasters, face renewed threats from this year’s developing El Niño as incomplete flood defences and government relocation schemes fuel fears of displacement and deepen a climate justice crisis.
paragraphs.zh: 如今，阿雷格里港受洪水影响的社区虽然仍在从巴西最致命的自然灾害之一中恢复，却因今年正在发展的厄尔尼诺而面临新的威胁：防洪设施不完善以及政府的搬迁安置计划，引发了民众对流离失所的担忧，并加深了气候正义危机。

paragraphs.en: Sarandi, along with other poorer areas of the city, is one such example. Despite being among those who are the least responsible for the emissions that cause climate breakdown, people there experienced the worst effects of the 2024 flood.
paragraphs.zh: 萨兰迪和该市其他较贫困地区就是这样的例子。尽管这些地区的人们对造成气候恶化的排放责任最小，他们却在2024年洪灾中承受了最严重的后果。
